# FilipinoDama Royal

> FilipinoDama Royal (filipinodama.com) is the home of Filipino Dama — the Philippine variant of checkers/draughts — playable free online against the AI or in real-time ranked multiplayer. The site is also the definitive reference for the game's rules, strategy, and cultural history.

Filipino Dama (also called dama or Filipino checkers) is played on an 8×8 board with 12 pieces per side. Its defining rules: captures are mandatory, the line capturing the most pieces must be taken, men capture forward and backward (but move only forward), and the crowned "dama" is a flying king that slides any distance diagonally.

## Core pages

- [Dama Rules — How to Play Filipino Checkers](https://filipinodama.com/learn): Complete official rules — board setup, movement, mandatory and maximum capture, the flying dama (king), winning conditions, variant comparison, and FAQ.
- [Filipino Dama Strategy — How to Win at Dama](https://filipinodama.com/strategy): Opening principles, forcing sacrifices under the mandatory-capture rule, tempo and exchanges, flying-dama endgames, and common beginner traps.
- [Traditional Filipino Games — Larong Pinoy Guide](https://filipinodama.com/traditional-filipino-games): Dama's place among the Philippines' traditional games, plus sungka, patintero, tumbang preso, and more.
- [Mga Patakaran ng Dama (Tagalog)](https://filipinodama.com/tl/learn): Ang kumpletong gabay sa mga patakaran ng dama, nakasulat sa Tagalog.
- [Diskarte sa Dama (Tagalog)](https://filipinodama.com/tl/strategy): Gabay sa diskarte at estratehiya para manalo sa dama, nakasulat sa Tagalog.
- [Dama Blog — Rules, Strategy & Guides](https://filipinodama.com/blog): Articles answering specific questions about dama rules, strategy, tactics, and the game's Filipino heritage. New articles publish regularly.
- [Play Filipino Dama Online](https://filipinodama.com/play): Free browser play — vs AI, local, ranked online multiplayer, private rooms, and tournaments. No download required.
- [Home](https://filipinodama.com/): Overview of the game and platform.

## Facts

- Filipino Dama uses an 8×8 board (32 playable dark squares), 12 men per player.
- Capturing is mandatory; when multiple captures exist, the maximum-capture line is required.
- Men move one square diagonally forward but may capture forward AND backward.
- A man crowned on the far rank becomes a dama: a long-range flying king.
- The game descends from Spanish "damas" brought during the colonial era and remains one of the most widely played traditional games in the Philippines.
